title: TIFF OPENING NIGHT!! 🎬✨ What a way to kick off my very first @TIFF! A...
transcript: I started out day one of TIFF by picking out my favourite criteria movies and ended it by dancing at an after after party. But so much happened in between. So let's rewind. Day one of the Toronto International Film Festival started bright and early with a trip to a dream location for any film nerd, the Criterion Collection. Now, I have spent years watching videos and seeing photos of my favourite actors and directors making their criterion picks, and I have always wondered what picks I would make myself, and today I finally got to do that. The video is already up, but I love this place. From there, I went to wander down King Street to check out all the TIFF activation, stopped by the official store because obviously I needed some merch, and grabbed lunch with a few new creator friends. But then it was time to start getting ready for opening night. I cannot believe I get to experience TIFF opening night with TikTok. Because I was a little bit nervous, I decided to treat myself and get a little glam. So glad I did. It made me feel so confident before we had three back to back events. I got to meet the entire TikTok cohort. They're all so nice and everyone looked amazing. Amazing. We all walked together down to the opening night reception and the energy of the city was just incredible. There were fans and movies and cameras and red carpets everywhere. we were headed to the Shangri LA for the pre opening cocktail party. We got photos on the carpet. Everything was so beautiful. It was so fun to talk to everybody about the week ahead. There was amazing food, including an oyster bar. And the party just flew by and it was finally time for my first film of TIFF. This is the reason that I'm here. I was so excited for the movies to begin. And we were at Roy Thompson Hall for the opening night of Being Human, directed by Sean Hayter, who directed Oscar winning film Kota. Also. A picture of my face appeared before the movie. I screamed. Anyway, being human tells the story of legendary disability rights activist Judy Heumann, who helped lead the fight for the signing of Section 5 0 4, a pivotal chapter of disability rights history that not enough people know about. I really love this movie. I think it is so funny and moving. There was a really great talk back after the film. Just an incredible reminder that collective action can actually change things. That people protested and organized and refused to be ignored, and the law did change. Anyway, I have a lot more to say about this film. Full video to come. We then all hopped on a shuttle to head to the official TIFF opening night party. We got to walk a red carpet. I felt very fancy. This venue was massive. There were so Many different, and they all had different vibes. I finally got to try cheese wheel pasta. So exciting. And I just had so much fun dancing and meeting new friends, and I was not ready for the night to end. So we did stop by the after after party, but only for a little bit because it is day one and this week is just beginning, and I have an entire film festival to go.
